sources.articleTitle: Microsoft warns Outlook, Teams users against fake outage emails
Kerala Police warns of fake traffic fine SMS scams

headline: Authorities Issue Warnings Regarding Growing Phishing Scams In India
seoTitle: Rising Phishing Scams Targeted In India
metaDescription: Indian authorities and tech firms warn of rising phishing campaigns, including fraudulent traffic fine SMS and fake service outage notifications.
aiSummaryBullets: Kerala Police reported fraudsters are distributing SMS alerts that falsely claim traffic violations to solicit fraudulent payments.
Microsoft issued a warning concerning phishing emails impersonating official service health alerts for Outlook and Teams users.
Officials recommend users verify all notifications through official administrative channels and avoid clicking suspicious links.
aiContextParagraph: Security authorities and major technology providers have identified an uptick in targeted phishing attempts aimed at users in India. The Kerala Police recently alerted the public to a scam involving deceptive text messages that falsely allege traffic infractions captured by camera systems, directing individuals to malicious payment links. Concurrently, Microsoft has raised alarms regarding cybercriminals exploiting service disruption reports to conduct phishing attacks against Outlook and Teams customers. These fraudulent messages often mimic legitimate service health notifications and threaten to delete user data if immediate action is not taken via an external link. Cybersecurity experts and corporate entities advise that individuals and organizations verify the legitimacy of any digital alerts by accessing their official admin centers directly rather than interacting with suspicious emails or text messages, which are designed to harvest credentials or sensitive financial information.
whyItIsViral: The story gained moderate traction as multiple major news outlets simultaneously reported on distinct, widespread digital security threats impacting the public.
